 <BODY BGCOLOR="WHITE" STYLE="line-height:Normal">

<Center><DIV STYLE="width:8.5in" align="left">
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="right"><B>Exhibit 99.1 </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:24pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="center"><B>FIDELITY NATIONAL INFORMATION SERVICES, INC. </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="center"><B>COMBINED COMPANY PRELIMINARY SUPPLEMENTAL INFORMATION &#8211; UNAUDITED </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>Issuer Solutions Business Acquisition and Worldpay Disposition </I></B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">On January&nbsp;9, 2026, Fidelity National Information Services, Inc., a Georgia corporation (&#8220;FIS&#8221; or the &#8220;Company&#8221;), completed its
previously announced (i)&nbsp;acquisition of the Issuer Solutions business (the &#8220;Issuer Solutions Business&#8221; or &#8220;Issuer Solutions&#8221;) from Global Payments Inc., a Georgia corporation (&#8220;Global Payments&#8221;), and
(ii)&nbsp;sale of all of its equity interests in Worldpay Holdco, LLC, a Delaware limited liability company (&#8220;Worldpay&#8221;), pursuant to the transaction agreement (the &#8220;FIS Transaction Agreement&#8221;) entered into on April&nbsp;17,
2025, by and among FIS, Global Payments, Total System Services LLC, a Delaware limited liability company (the &#8220;Purchased Entity&#8221;), and Worldpay. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Concurrently with the consummation of the transactions contemplated by the FIS Transaction Agreement, Global Payments completed the acquisition of 100% of the
issued and outstanding equity interests of Worldpay that were not owned by FIS, pursuant to the transaction agreement (the &#8220;GTCR Transaction Agreement&#8221; and together with the FIS Transaction Agreement, the &#8220;Transaction
Agreements&#8221;), entered into on April&nbsp;17, 2025, by and among Global Payments, Worldpay, certain affiliates of GTCR LLC (&#8220;GTCR&#8221;) and certain other parties thereto. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Upon the terms and subject to the conditions set forth in the FIS Transaction Agreement, FIS acquired from Global Payments the Issuer Solutions Business
through the acquisition of 100% of the issued and outstanding equity interests of the Purchased Entity (the &#8220;Issuer Solutions Acquisition&#8221;). As consideration for the Issuer Solutions Acquisition, FIS (i)&nbsp;sold to Global Payments its
remaining equity interests in Worldpay (the &#8220;Worldpay Disposition&#8221;) and (ii)&nbsp;paid approximately $7.7&nbsp;billion in cash, representing the excess of the purchase price payable by FIS in respect of the Issuer Solutions Acquisition
over the purchase price payable by Global Payments in respect of the Worldpay Disposition. The cash payment amount is subject to customary post-closing adjustments in respect of the respective purchase price for each of Worldpay and the Issuer
Solutions Business. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The purchase price paid by Global Payments in respect of Worldpay was based on a $24.25&nbsp;billion enterprise valuation of Worldpay,
and the purchase price paid by FIS in respect of the Issuer Solutions Business was based on a $13.5&nbsp;billion enterprise valuation of the Issuer Solutions Business, in each case, subject to customary adjustments for the cash, debt and working
capital (relative to a target) of Worldpay and the Issuer Solutions Business, respectively, as of the closing of the transactions contemplated by the FIS Transaction Agreement and the GTCR Transaction Agreement (the &#8220;Closing&#8221;). </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Following the Closing, the results of operations and financial position of the Issuer Solutions Business will be included in the consolidated results of FIS
from and after the date of acquisition, and FIS will no longer recognize its equity method investment in Worldpay. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>Supplemental Financial Data
</I></B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Due to the financial impact of the transactions described above, FIS management desires to furnish investors with the additional information set
forth herein to improve the understanding of the Company&#8217;s operating performance. The purpose of the schedules included in this Exhibit 99.1 is to recalculate certain <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-GAAP</FONT> measures of the
Company&#8217;s historical financial performance on an adjusted combined company basis for the fiscal years ended December&nbsp;31, 2024 and 2025, and the related quarters for 2025. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Company has derived certain <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-GAAP</FONT> measures from unaudited pro forma condensed combined financial information of
FIS and the Issuer Solutions Business and notes thereto prepared in accordance with Article 11 of Regulation <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">S-X</FONT> for the year ended December 31, 2025 in Exhibit 99.2 to the Company&#8217;s Current Report on
Form <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">8-K/A</FONT> filed on February 24, 2026. This Exhibit 99.1 to this Current Report on Form <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">8-K</FONT> includes certain <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-GAAP</FONT> measures
that are not in conformity with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles (&#8220;GAAP&#8221;), including Adjusted Combined EBITDA and Adjusted Combined EBITDA Margin. The content of the Exhibits are as follows: </P>
<P STYLE="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">

including combined company <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-GAAP</FONT> adjustments; </P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

segment basis under the new segment reporting structure that the Company is expected to use on a <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">go-forward</FONT> basis. As a result of the Company&#8217;s acquisition of the Issuer Solutions Business, the Company
expects to reorganize its reportable segments to include the Issuer Solutions Business within the Banking Solutions segment and to move certain of the Company&#8217;s existing business lines between Banking Solutions, Capital Market Solutions and
the Corporate and Other segment. </P></TD></TR></TABLE>
</DIV></Center>

<Center><DIV STYLE="width:8.5in" align="left">
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The unaudited adjusted combined financial information is presented for illustrative purposes only and does
not reflect the financial results of the combined companies had the companies actually been combined at the beginning of the periods presented and is not necessarily indicative of the future results of operations of the Company. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>FIS Use of <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Non-GAAP</FONT> Financial Information </I></B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">GAAP is the term used to refer to the standard framework of guidelines for financial accounting in the United States. GAAP includes the standards, conventions,
and rules accountants follow in recording and summarizing transactions and in the preparation of financial statements. In addition to reporting financial results in accordance with GAAP, we have provided certain
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-GAAP</FONT> financial measures. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">These <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-GAAP</FONT> measures include Adjusted
Combined EBITDA and Adjusted Combined EBITDA Margin. These <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-GAAP</FONT> measures may be used in this release and/or in the attached supplemental financial information. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">We believe these <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-GAAP</FONT> measures help investors better understand the underlying fundamentals of our business. As
further described below, the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-GAAP</FONT> earnings measures presented eliminate items management believes are not indicative of FIS&#8217; operating performance. For these reasons, management also uses these <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-GAAP</FONT> measures in its assessment and management of FIS&#8217; performance. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Adjusted Combined EBITDA </B>reflects
net earnings (loss) before interest, other income (expense), taxes, equity method investment earnings (loss), and depreciation and amortization, and excludes certain costs that do not constitute normal, recurring, cash operating expenses on a total
company combined basis. These excluded costs generally include purchase price amortization of acquired intangible assets, as well as acquisition, integration and certain other costs and asset impairments. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Adjusted Combined EBITDA Margin </B>reflects Adjusted Combined EBITDA, as defined above, divided by Pro Forma Combined Revenue. </P>
</DIV></Center>


<p style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"> </p>

<Center><DIV STYLE="width:8.5in" align="left">
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="center"><B>FIDELITY NATIONAL INFORMATION SERVICES, INC. </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="center"><B>COMBINED COMPANY PRELIMINARY SUPPLEMENTAL INFORMATION &#8211; UNAUDITED </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Notes to Exhibit A and B </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">(a) Quarterization of
FIS&#8217; annual unaudited pro forma condensed combined statements of earnings (loss) for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2025. The annual unaudited pro forma condensed combined statements of earnings (loss) for the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2025 was prepared in accordance with Article 11 of Regulation <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">S-X</FONT> in Exhibit 99.2 to the Company&#8217;s Current Report on Form <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">8-K/A</FONT> filed on February&nbsp;24, 2026, to
which represents the historical consolidated statements of earnings of FIS and the combined statements of income of the Issuer Solutions Business giving effect to the transactions as if they had occurred on January&nbsp;1, 2025. Additionally, the
2024 annual period was prepared in accordance with Article 11 of Regulation <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">S-X</FONT> as if the transactions occurred on January&nbsp;1, 2024. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">(b) This item represents purchase price amortization expense on all intangible assets acquired through various acquisitions including the preliminary amounts
estimated for the Issuer Solutions Business acquisition, including customer relationships, contract value, trademarks and tradenames, <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-compete</FONT> agreements and technology assets acquired. The Company has
excluded the impact of purchase accounting amortization of intangibles as such amounts can be significantly impacted by the timing and/or size of acquisitions. Although the Company excludes these amounts from its
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-GAAP</FONT> expenses, the Company believes that it is important for investors to understand that such intangible assets contribute to revenue generation. Purchase accounting amortization of intangible assets will
recur in future periods until such intangible assets have been fully amortized. Any future acquisitions may result in purchase price amortization of future intangible assets. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">(c) These items represent the reversal of corporate allocations to the Issuer Solutions Business under periods of Global Payments ownership not expected to
recur following the Issuer Solutions Business acquisition, partially offset by expected costs under transition services agreements and corporate overhead. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">(d) This item represents the expected stock-based compensation to employees of the Issuer Solutions Business. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">(e) Acquisition, integration, and other costs include expenses incurred by both FIS and the Issuer Solutions Business in connection with completed and pending
acquisitions, integration of acquired businesses, enterprise transformation initiatives (including platform modernization), severance and termination costs, separation of the Worldpay Merchant Solutions business, incremental stock-based compensation
related to specific programs, divestiture-related costs, and other enterprise cost control and strategic initiatives. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">(f) There were no material
impairments during the quarterly and <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap"><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">year-to-date</FONT></FONT> periods for fiscal year 2025. The year ended December&nbsp;31, 2024 included impairments primarily related to the
termination of certain internally developed software projects. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">(g) This item represents historical FIS costs that were incurred in support of the Worldpay
Merchant Solutions business prior to the separation but are not directly attributable to it and thus were not recorded in discontinued operations. The Company was reimbursed for these expenses as part of transition services agreements and/or
eliminated them post separation; therefore, the expenses have been adjusted out of continuing operations and added to discontinued operations. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">(h) The
Issuer Solutions Business has been included within the Banking Solutions segment within Payments. </P>
